introduction: WorkForce West Virginia administers unemployment insurance for eligible workers. File an initial claim, enroll in Job Service and continue weekly certifications while eligibility is reviewed.

who: Workers with sufficient covered wages and a qualifying separation who meet weekly eligibility requirements.
Claimants generally must be available for full-time work and actively seek it; the agency lists specific work-search exceptions.
sections.get: Weekly temporary income based on the wage record and eligible claim weeks. A monetary determination shows potential benefits and is not an approval.
sections.docs: Prepare employment history, dates and reasons for separation, identity information and wage records. Keep proof of each job search activity and records of work and earnings during claimed weeks.
sections.apply:
1. Go to uc.workforcewv.org and select the new or additional unemployment claim option.
  2. Enroll in WorkForce West Virginia Job Service as required.
  3. Submit weekly certifications for each prior week claimed and report all earnings.
  4. Ask the agency promptly about an incorrect or missing wage record.
sections.after: Complete four weekly work search activities unless an applicable exception is confirmed. Retain proof for the benefit year plus six months; uploads during weekly certification are available. Claim the unpaid waiting week and read decisions for appeal deadlines.

faqs: No; it explains potential amounts based on wages.
How many work search activities are required?
The current agency guidance lists four per week unless an applicable exception applies.
Yes, the agency offers upload during weekly certification.
Must I report tips and commissions?
The agency requires reporting all work and earnings for the claim week.
Do I need to claim the waiting week?
Yes, it must be claimed to receive waiting-week credit even though it is unpaid.
